Pan Y, Jin H, Chen W, Yu Z, Ye T, Zheng Y, et al. conducted a study on the use of docetaxel with or without zoledronic acid in patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer, published in the International Urology and Nephrology journal in 2014 (Volume 46, Pages 2319–2326). 2. Paterson AH, Powles TJ, Kanis JA, McCloskey E, Hanson J, Ashley S. performed a double-blind controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of oral clodronate in patients with bone metastases from breast cancer. This study was published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology in 1993 (Volume 11, Pages 59–65). 3. Piga A, Bracci R, Ferretti B, Sandri P, Nortilli R, Acito L, et al. conducted a double-blind randomized study on oral clodronate for treating bone metastases from tumors that are poorly responsive to chemotherapy. The findings were published in the Journal of Experimental Clinical Cancer Research in 1998 (Volume 17, Pages 213–217). 4. Robertson AG, Reed NS, Ralston SH. investigated the effect of oral clodronate on metastatic bone pain in a double-blind, placebo-controlled study. The results were published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology in 1995 (Volume 13, Pages 2427–2430). 5. Rosen LS, Gordon D, Tchekmedyian S, Yanagihara R, Hirsh V, Krzakowski M, et al. compared zoledronic acid versus placebo in treating skeletal metastases in patients with lung cancer and other solid tumors. This Phase III, double-blind, randomized trial was published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology in 2003 (Volume 21, Pages 3150–3157). 6. Siris ES, Hyman GA, Canfield RE. studied the effects of dichloromethylene diphosphonate in women with breast carcinoma metastatic to the skeleton. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Medicine in 1983 (Volume 74, Pages 401–406). 7. Small EJ, Smith MR, Seaman JJ, Petrone S, Kowalski MO. conducted a combined analysis of two multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled studies on pamidronate disodium for palliating bone pain in men with metastatic prostate cancer. The results were published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology in 2003 (Volume 21, Pages 4277–4284). 8. Smith J Jr. evaluated the palliative effects of sodium etidronate on painful bone metastases from prostate cancer in a randomized, prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. The findings were published in the Journal of Urology in 1989 (Volume 141, Pages 85–87). 9. Smith MR, Halabi S, Ryan CJ, Hussain A, Vogelzang N, Stadler W, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial on early zoledronic acid use in men with castration-sensitive prostate cancer and bone metastases. The results of CALGB 90202 (Alliance) were published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology in 2014 (Volume 32, Pages 1143–1150). 10. Theriault RL, Lipton A, Hortobagyi GN, Leff R, Glück S, Stewart JF, et al. demonstrated that pamidronate reduces skeletal morbidity in women with advanced breast cancer and lytic bone lesions in a randomized, placebo-controlled trial. This study was part of Protocol 18 of the Aredia Breast Cancer Study Group and was published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology in 1999 (Volume 17, Pages 846–854). 11. Tripathy D, Lichinitzer M, Lazarev A, MacLachlan SA, Apffelstaedt J, Budde M, et al. assessed the efficacy and safety of oral ibandronate for treating metastatic bone disease in breast cancer. The results of this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial were published in Annals of Oncology in 2004 (Volume 15, Pages 743–750). 12. Tubiana-Hulin M, Beuzeboc P, Mauriac L, Barbet N, Frenay M, Monnier A, et al. conducted a double-blinded controlled study comparing clodronate versus placebo in patients with breast cancer bone metastases. The findings were published in Bulletin du Cancer in 2001 (Volume 88, Pages 701–707). 13. Ueno S, Mizokami A, Fukagai T, Fujimoto N, Oh-Oka H, Kondo Y, et al. evaluated the efficacy of combined androgen blockade with zoledronic acid in prostate cancer patients with bone metastases. This study, known as the ZABTON-PC trial, was published in Anticancer Research in 2013 (Volume 33, Pages 3837–3844). 14. van Holten-Verzantvoort AT, Bijvoet OLM, Hermans J, Harinck HIJ, Elte JWF, Beex LVAM, et al. reported reduced morbidity from skeletal metastases in breast cancer patients during long-term bisphosphonate (APD) treatment. The study was published in The Lancet in 1987 (Volume 330, Pages 983–985). 15. van Holten-Verzantvoort AT, Kroon HM, Bijvoet OL, Cleton FJ, Beex LV, Blijham G, et al. investigated palliative pamidronate treatment in patients with bone metastases from breast cancer. The findings were published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology in 1993 (Volume 11, Pages 491–498). 16. Vinholes J, Purohit O, Abbey M, Eastell R, Coleman R. explored the relationship between biochemical and symptomatic responses in a double-blind randomized trial of pamidronate for metastatic bone disease. The results were published in Annals of Oncology in 1997 (Volume 8, Pages 1243–1250). 17. Wang Y, Tao H, Yu X, Wang Z, Wang M. examined the clinical significance of zoledronic acid and strontium-89 in patients with asymptomatic bone metastases from non-small-cell lung cancer. The study was published in Clinical Lung Cancer in 2013 (Volume 14, Pages 254–260). 18. WHO guidelines emphasize the importance of pharmacological and radiotherapeutic management of cancer pain in adults and adolescents. These guidelines highlight the need for individualized pain assessment and management strategies based on the severity and underlying causes of pain. 19. The Brief Pain Inventory (BPI) is a widely used tool for assessing pain intensity, location, and its impact on daily activities. It has been validated in multiple languages and is applicable to both malignant and non-malignant pain conditions. 20. The Critical Care Pain Observation Tool (CPOT) and the Pain Assessment in Advanced Dementia (PAINAD) are specialized tools designed to evaluate pain in non-communicative or critically ill patients, ensuring evidence-based pain management in these populations.
